subject: Secure SDLC evidence: PR review logs, CI approvals, and secrets custody (BlueStone assessment)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Gina Morales <gina.morales@acme-assess.com>, sig@bluestone.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Secure SDLC evidence: PR review logs, CI approvals, and secrets custody (BlueStone assessment)

Hi Gina / BlueStone team,

Thanks for the checklist you sent over. Per your request we pulled together an initial proofpack that shows how Redwood enforces secure SDLC controls for production-facing model-serving code. High level: code review gating, CI approval workflow, ephemeral credential use, KMS-backed secret rotation, and change approvals with traceability.

I uploaded a zipped bundle with representative artifacts to the shared Drive (link below) and included a CSV of CI approval events for the last 90 days. The bundle contains: PR export (including mandatory reviewer stamps), CI run logs for canary and prod deploys, the change approval ticket exports, and our secrets rotation summary.

Quick notes on what to look for:
- PR policy: all prod-affecting PRs require two approvers, at least one from infra/security.
- CI: approvals are captured in the pipeline as an immutable approval event (job: manual-approve-prod), and are exported in ci-approval-audit-20270329.csv.
- Secrets: we rotate the model-serving KMS keys quarterly; application secrets are scoped as short-lived tokens minted via the EPHEM token service (RB-3456).

Attachments: redwood_sdlc_proofpack_v1.zip (zip), ci-approval-audit-20270329.csv (csv), kms-rotation-summary-202701.pdf (pdf)

Let me know if you want an extracted set focused only on production model-serving pipelines (we can filter). If useful, we can set up a 30-min walkthrough with Irene and Kim to review artifact provenance.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Principal PM, Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Gina Morales <gina.morales@acme-assess.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC evidence: PR review logs, CI approvals, and secrets custody (BlueStone assessment)

Thanks Jordan — received the bundle and started a quick triage. A couple of follow-ups from our initial pass:

1) Can you provide a short mapping doc that ties each artifact back to the SIG/SOC2 control IDs? We need to show explicit control coverage.
2) For the CSV of CI approvals, can you include the pipeline job IDs and the SHA of the triggering commit for each approval row?
3) We saw references to RB-3456 in a few artifacts — please confirm whether RB-3456 is the single source of truth for ephemeral token issuance and, if so, provide the ticket history for token provisioning changes.
4) Finally, for the KMS rotation summary: can you confirm whether rotation is automated and include the last manual rotation approval (if any) and the approver identity?

If you can get these clarifications/files by Wednesday EOD we can keep to our review timeline. If not, please propose the earliest you can.

—Gina
Senior Assessor, Acme Assessment Services

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Gina Morales <gina.morales@acme-assess.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC evidence: PR review logs, CI approvals, and secrets custody (BlueStone assessment)

Gina — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, full artifacts attached / linked below.

1) Mapping doc: attached file "sdlc_control_mapping_20270330.pdf" (excerpted mapping of artifacts to SIG/SOC2 control IDs: CC6.1, CC7.2, and CW-3 equivalents).
2) CI CSV: we regenerated ci-approval-audit-20270329.csv with two added columns (pipeline_job_id, commit_sha). See attachment and also the Drive export row-level provenance.
3) RB-3456: correct — RB-3456 is the Jira epic for EPHEM token service. Attached "rb-3456-change-history.txt" with timestamps and approver names for issuance policy changes. The issuance service is triggered by CI during ephemeral credential bake steps and tenants request short-lived tokens via our internal auth service.
4) KMS rotation: rotation is automated via our KMS operator; man-made rotations are rare. The last manual rotation was 2026-12-11 and was approved by Kim Park (kimberly.park@redwood.com). See kms-rotation-summary-202701.pdf for the automated rotation schedule and logs.

I also included a PR export (pr-review-export-202703.zip) and a filtered list of production deploy approvals (prod-approvals-202701-202703.csv). If you need GPG-signed commit proofs or a separate s3 manifest of the artifacts, let us know.

Irene Choi
Director, Engineering Security
Redwood Inference

From: Gina Morales <gina.morales@acme-assess.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 16:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Secure SDLC evidence: PR review logs, CI approvals, and secrets custody (BlueStone assessment)

Team — this is excellent, thank you. The mapping doc and the regenerated CSVs give us the coverage we needed to tie artifacts back to SOC2/SIG controls. A couple minor follow-ups and then we should be able to close the request:

- Please add the verifier identity (internal service account) used to sign the CSV export for chain-of-custody.
- For one PR in the export we observed an approval from an account that no longer exists (internal handle: old-sre). Can you confirm if that approval was from a deactivated account and provide who approved on the deactivation path?

If you can drop a short note on both items by end of day Friday we'll close on our side and proceed to the formal assessment write-up.

Best,
Gina
Senior Assessor, Acme Assessment Services

On Wed, 31 Mar 2027 at 17:12 Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Gina — we'll get those two follow-ups done.
>
> Action items:
> - Kimberly will confirm verifier service account name and attach the signed export.
> - Irene / Lauren will trace the "old-sre" approval and provide the deactivation/approval history.
>
> I'll capture these in RB-3456 and update the Drive folder with the signed CSV and a short investigator note.
>
> Jordan

> Redwood Inference
